links.outcome: Prediction ROC-AUC under synthetically perturbed (misspelled, missing whitespace) clinical text at 5-20% error rates
links.effect: Models tolerant to error rates <10% but performance declined significantly at ≥10%; embedding features with XGBoost were more sensitive at <10%; AACH ROC-AUC difference after correction 0.002-0.004.
links.quote: Although the performance in terms of ROC-AUC is tolerant to small error rates (<10%), it starts to be significant with a high error rate (≥10%).

links.outcome: Accuracy of Mixtral error detection in progress notes against manual ground truth
links.effect: Mixtral overestimated errors, misclassified medical terms as misspellings and hallucinated misspellings; correctly identified errors in 45% of notes (63% in abstract/discussion); 2.95% mean deviation from ground truth.
links.quote: Qualitative analysis of the results revealed that Mixtral erroneously identified medical terminologies (eg, ATOR, ADL, Perianal, situ, mane, obs, RN, etc) as misspelled tokens.

links.outcome: Performance of feature and model choices
links.effect: TF-IDF outperformed embedding features across both datasets; model effectiveness varied by task.
links.quote: Across both datasets, term frequency-inverted document frequency outperformed embedding features, and machine learning models varied in effectiveness, highlighting that optimal feature representation and model choice depend on the specific task.

links.outcome: Predictive model performance under varying token-level error rates
links.effect: Models were tolerant to lower error rates (<10%), but predictive performance declined significantly as error rates increased to 10% or higher.
links.quote: This study revealed that models performed relatively well on datasets with lower error rates (<10%), but their performance declined significantly as error rates increased (≥10%).

links.outcome: Predictive performance of complex embedding models versus simpler models
links.effect: TF-IDF models outperformed neural network-based embedding models including word2vec, ClinicalBERT, and BioClinical ModernBERT across datasets, with logistic regression having comparatively higher ROC-AUC for most representations.
links.quote: In terms of the feature representation models, TF-IDF models outperformed neural network–based embedding models (word2vec, ClinicalBERT, and BioClinical ModernBERT).
